# ------- RQ1: HOW DOES CHILDREN'S BEHAVIOR VARY BY AGE & COUNTRY?

```{r data entry, include = FALSE}
x <- read_csv("tbxc_finaldata_oct15.csv", na = "")
```


```{r new variables, include = F}
x$country <- factor(x$country, 
                               levels = c("Ecuador", "Peru", 
                                          "Uganda", "Canada", "USA"))


x$age.integer <- factor(x$age.year)
x$is.honest <- x$honesty.numreturned
x$is.honest[x$honesty.numreturned>0] <- 1
x$is.honest[x$honesty.numreturned==0] <- 0

legendtitle <- "Country"


## Setting colors & color palette
colorpalette <- c("#3B40B8", "#61C76D", "#C74726", "#E6B89F", "#81B7BD")

color.Ecuador <- "#3B40B8"
color.Peru <- "#61C76D"
color.Uganda <- "#C74726"
color.USA <- "#81B7BD"
color.Canada <- "#E6B89F"
  
x$order <- as.factor(x$order)
```


## Descriptives & Overview

```{r descriptives}

# Total sample
x %>% 
  tally()

# Total sample, gender
x %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% 
  tally()


# Sample sizes by country
x %>% 
  group_by(country) %>% 
  tally()


x %>% 
  group_by(country, age.group) %>% 
  tally()

x %>% 
  group_by(country, count.sixtokens, age.year) %>% 
  tally()

# Gender by country
x %>% 
  group_by(country, gender) %>% 
  tally()

# Ages by country
x %>% 
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(tibble(mean.age= mean(age.year), sd.age = sd(age.year)))

# Ages in general
x %>% 
  summarise(tibble(mean.age= mean(age.year), sd.age = sd(age.year)))
```




## TASK BATTERY - HONESTY

### Honesty Data Viz
```{r honesty density, echo = F}

plot.honesty.density <- 
  ggplot(x, aes(x=honesty.numreturned, y = country)) + 
     geom_density_ridges(aes(fill= country, color = country, alpha = 0.9),
                      quantile_lines=TRUE,
                      quantile_fun=function(x,...)mean(x)) +
  xlab("\n Total Starbursts Returned") + ylab("Density\n") + 
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  theme(text = element_text(size=19))  +
  scale_fill_manual(legendtitle, 
                    values = colorpalette) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "black", "black", "black", "black"), 
                     guide = "none") +  theme(legend.position = "none") +
   scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0,1,2,3))
plot.honesty.density

```


```{r honesty by age & country, echo = F}

plot.honesty.agexc <- ggplot(x, aes(x=age.year, y=honesty.numreturned, fill = country)) + 
  geom_smooth(alpha = 0.2, aes(colour=country), method = "lm") +
  geom_line(stat = "smooth", method = "lm", aes(colour=country), 
            size = 1.5) +
  xlab("\n Age") +
  ylab("Number of Resources Returned \n") + theme_gray() + 
  theme(text = element_text(size=19)) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), 
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  theme(text = element_text(size=19)) + ylim(-.3,3)  +
  scale_fill_manual(legendtitle, 
                    values = colorpalette) + 
  scale_color_manual(legendtitle, 
                     values = colorpalette) 
plot.honesty.agexc

```

### HONESTY: Models

```{r honesty models lm}
## PRE-REGISTERED MODEL FOR HONESTY 
honesty.mod.intxn.lm <-  lm(honesty.numreturned ~ age.year*country,
                            data = x)
summary(honesty.mod.intxn.lm)

honesty.mod.maineff.lm <- lm(honesty.numreturned ~ age.year + country, 
                             data = x)
summary(honesty.mod.maineff.lm)

anova(honesty.mod.intxn.lm, honesty.mod.maineff.lm, test = "Chisq")
# Significant two-way interaction between country * age.
## But issues with linear separability of Ecuador

## Better to use linear probability model
plot(honesty.mod.intxn.lm)

## LPM for honesty is a better fit for the data, which is clearly bimodal
## Now using a binary variable "is.honest", reported in ms as deviating from pre-reg
## ------------------FINAL MODEL FOR HONESTY  ------------------------
honesty.mod.intxn.lpm <-  lm(is.honest ~ age.year*country,
                             data = x)
summary(honesty.mod.intxn.lpm)

honesty.mod.maineff.lpm <-  lm(is.honest ~ age.year + country,
                               data = x)
summary(honesty.mod.maineff.lpm)


## Honesty Order Effects
honesty.mod.maineff.lpm.oe <-  lm(is.honest ~ age.year + country +
                                 order, data = x)
summary(honesty.mod.maineff.lpm.oe)
## No order effects

anova(honesty.mod.maineff.lpm, honesty.mod.intxn.lpm,test = "Chisq")
## Trending two-way interaction

honesty.mod.intxn.lpm.justage <-  lm(is.honest ~ age.year,data = x)
summary(honesty.mod.intxn.lpm.justage)

```

### TRUST: Models

```{r trust models}
## ------------------ FINAL MODEL FOR TRUST ------------------------
trust.mod.intx <-  lm(trust.numshared ~ age.year*country, data = x)
summary(trust.mod.intx)

trust.mod.maineff <- lm(trust.numshared ~ age.year + country, data = x)
summary(trust.mod.maineff)

anova(trust.mod.maineff, trust.mod.intx, test = "Chisq")
# Significant two-way interaction between country * age.

broom::tidy(trust.mod.intx, conf.int=TRUE) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 9)

trust.mod.maineff.justage <- lm(trust.numshared ~ age.year , data = x)
summary(trust.mod.maineff.justage)


## Order effects for trust

trust.mod.maineff.oe <- lm(trust.numshared ~ age.year + country +
                          order, data = x)
summary(trust.mod.maineff.oe)
```

## STANDARD ADVANTAGEOUS INEQUITY (4-1)

```{r data cleaning for standard ai, echo = F}

x.long.dist <- melt(data = x, measure.vars = c("tt1.trialtype",
                                                 "tt2.trialtype",
                                                 "tt3.trialtype",
                                                 "tt4.trialtype",
                                                 "tt5.trialtype",
                                                 "tt6.trialtype"),
                     variable.name = "test.trial.number",
                     value.name = "dist")


x.long.dec <- melt(data = x, measure.vars = c("tt1.response",
                                                "tt2.response",
                                                "tt3.response",
                                                "tt4.response",
                                                "tt5.response",
                                                "tt6.response"),
                    variable.name = "trial.dec",
                    value.name = "dec")

x.long <- x.long.dist
x.long$dec <- x.long.dec$dec

table(x.long$dist, x.long$dec)

x.long$dec <- gsub("Reject", "1", x.long$dec)
x.long$dec <- gsub("Accept", "0", x.long$dec)
x.long$dec <- as.numeric(x.long$dec)

```

```{r standard ai data cleanup, echo = F}

ai.summary <- summarySE(data = x.long, na.rm = TRUE,
                         measurevar = "dec",
                         groupvars = c("country", "dist", "age.year"))

ai.summary <- ai.summary[rowSums(is.na(ai.summary)) == 0,]
ai.summary 
ai.summary$dist <- factor(ai.summary$dist)

ai.only <- ai.summary[ai.summary$dist=="AI",]
eq.only <- ai.summary[ai.summary$dist=="EQ",]


ai.summary.noage <- summarySE(data = x.long, na.rm = TRUE,
                         measurevar = "dec",
                         groupvars = c("country", "dist"))

ai.summary.noage <- ai.summary.noage[rowSums(is.na(ai.summary.noage)) == 0,]
ai.summary.noage
ai.summary.noage$dist <- factor(ai.summary.noage$dist)
ai.summary.noage.aionly <- ai.summary.noage[ai.summary.noage$dist=="AI",]


x.long.ai <- x.long[x.long$dist=="AI",]

```

### STANDARD (4-1) ADVANTAGEOUS INEQUITY:  Model


```{r standard AI models}
## Binomial regression a la Blake 2015, but LPR (below) preferred analysis
fair.mod.intx.binom <-  glmer(dec ~ age.year*country + dist + (1|pid),
                      data = x.long,
                      glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", 
                                   optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)),
                      family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(fair.mod.intx.binom)

fair.mod.maineff.binom <-  glmer(dec ~ age.year + country + dist + (1|pid),
                      data = x.long,
                      glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", 
                                   optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)),
                      family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(fair.mod.maineff.binom)

anova(fair.mod.intx.binom, fair.mod.maineff.binom, test = "Chisq")
# Significant two-way interaction between country * age

```


```{r non-logistic regression standard ai}

## Linear probability model better model, as argued by Gomila 2021, described in ms
## ------------------ FINAL MODEL FOR AI ------------------------
fair.mod.intx <-  lmer(dec ~ age.year*country + dist + (1|pid),
                      data = x.long)

summary(fair.mod.intx)

fair.mod.maineff <-  lmer(dec ~ age.year + country + dist + (1|pid),
                      data = x.long)

summary(fair.mod.maineff)
anova(fair.mod.intx, fair.mod.maineff, test = "Chisq")
# Significant two-way interaction between country * age
```

```{r}
fair.mod.maineff.xai <-  lmer(dec ~  tt7.rejects + (1|pid),
                      data = x.long)
summary(fair.mod.maineff.xai)
```



```{r}
## Ecuadorean kids accept AI more with increasing age
ecukidsaccept <- x.long %>% 
  filter(country == "Ecuador", dist == "AI") %>%
```

# ------- RQ2: HOW DO CHILDREN'S BEHAVIORS IN THE TASKS CORRELATE WITH EACH OTHER?
## VIRTUE CORRELATIONS / FACTOR ANALYSIS

#### Factor Analysis
This is the intuitive approach: factor analyze behaviors across tasks. Theoretically, though, this doesn't capture what we care about, as we want to know how many types of strategies (e.g., regular combinations of behaviors across tasks) there are, not how many different types of tasks there are. In addition, practically, we don't have the sample to do country level factor analysis.

```{r}
## data prep

sum.inequity.score <- x.long %>% 
  group_by(pid, dist) %>% 
  summarise(reject.sum = sum(dec, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = pid,
              names_from = dist,
              values_from = reject.sum) %>% 
  select(-`NA`)

sum.inequity.score

x.for.cor <- right_join(sum.inequity.score, x, by = c("pid"))

x.for.cor <- x.for.cor %>% 
  rename(., Forgiveness = forg.givenback, 
         Trustworthiness = trust.numshared,
         Honesty = is.honest,
         `Extreme AI` = tt7.rejects)

df.for.factor <- x.for.cor %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(AI, Forgiveness, Trustworthiness, Honesty, `Extreme AI`) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>% # trimming to kids with all five data points
  scale(.) %>% 
  as_tibble()

```


```{r}
KMO_test <- KMO(df.for.factor)
print(KMO_test)

bartlett_test <- cortest.bartlett(df.for.factor)
print(bartlett_test)

fa <- fa.parallel(df.for.factor, fa = "fa", n.iter = 100)
### suggests one factor

factor.all <-   factanal(df.for.factor, factors = 1,  n.obs = nrow(.),
                         scores = "regression")
print(factor.all)


factor.plot <- x.for.cor %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(country, AI, Forgiveness, Trustworthiness, Honesty, `Extreme AI`) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>% # trimming to kids with all five data points %>% 
  bind_cols(factor.score = factor.all$scores) %>% 
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(factor.score), se = std.error(factor.score)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = country, y = mean, ymin = mean-1.96*se, ymax = mean+1.96*se,
             color = country)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, shape = 18) + 
  geom_errorbar(width = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Country", y = "Factor Score") +
  scale_color_manual(legendtitle, values = colorpalette) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

Here we visualize the correlation. 

```{r}

df.for.spearman <- x.for.cor %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(AI, Forgiveness, Trustworthiness, Honesty, `Extreme AI`) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>% 
  scale(.) %>% 
  cor(method = "spearman") 

## ggplot for all countries, spearman
corrplot.all <- df.for.spearman %>% 
  ggcorrplot(show.diag = F, type="lower", lab=TRUE, lab_size=4)+
  ggtitle("All Countries")
corrplot.all


```


## Cluster individuals by behavior
Because we want to know how many types of strategies (e.g., regular combinations of behaviors across tasks) there are, not how many different types of tasks there are, we want to use cluster analysis to group individuals by their behavior. 

```{r}
# create a scaled tibble with all behaviors plus country
x.for.cor.country <- x.for.cor %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(country, AI, Forgiveness, Trustworthiness, Honesty, `Extreme AI`) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>% # trimming to kids with all five data points %>%  
  mutate(across(-country, ~(.x-mean(.x))/sd(.x))) %>% 
  as_tibble() 

# cluster the observations and use the optimal cluster solution
opt_clust <- NbClust(data = df.for.factor,
                     distance = "euclidean",
                     method = "ward.D2",
                     min.nc = 2,
                     max.nc = 8,
                     index = "all")

clust_data <- bind_cols(x.for.cor.country, cluster.assignment = opt_clust$Best.partition)
                        
(clust_country <- clust_data %>% 
  group_by(country, cluster.assignment) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  group_by(country) %>% 
  mutate(prop = n/sum(n),
         cluster.assignment = factor(cluster.assignment,
                                     labels = c("Maximization",
                                                "Generic Cooperation",
                                                "Partner-Contingent Cooperation"))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = country, y = prop, color = cluster.assignment, fill = cluster.assignment)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percentage of Population", color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

```



### Map clusters to behavior
Now that we have clusters, we can look at the behaviors that characterize those clusters.

```{r}
clust_map <- x.for.cor %>% 
  select(pid,
         age.year,
         country,
         AI,
         `Extreme AI`,
         Forgiveness,
         Trustworthiness,
         Honesty) %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  bind_cols(cluster_assignment = clust_data$cluster.assignment) %>% 
  mutate(cluster_assignment = factor(cluster_assignment,
                                     levels = c(1:3),
                                     labels = c("Maximization",
                                                "Generic Cooperation",
                                                "Partner-Contingent Cooperation")))


clust_summary <- clust_map %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = AI:Honesty,
               names_to = "Task",
               values_to = "Behavior") %>% 
  group_by(cluster_assignment, Task) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(Behavior),
            se = std.error(Behavior),
            median = median(Behavior))

clust_mean <- ggplot(clust_summary, aes(x = Task, y = mean, color = cluster_assignment, ymin = mean-1.96*se, ymax = mean+1.96*se)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(alpha = .4, position = position_dodge(.9), width = .2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(color = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Mean Behavior") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~Task,
             scales = "free") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")

clust_med <- ggplot(clust_summary, aes(x = Task, y = median, color = cluster_assignment)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(.9)) +
  labs(color = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Median Behavior") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = c(.85, .2),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~Task,
             scales = "free") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")


clust_mean / clust_med
  
```

We can also visualize the same data by faceting on cluster and putting task on the x-axis.

```{r}

task_mean <- ggplot(clust_summary, aes(x = Task, y = mean, color = Task, ymin = mean-1.96*se, ymax = mean+1.96*se)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(alpha = .4, position = position_dodge(.9), width = .2, show.legend = FALSE) +

task_mean + task_med + guide_area() + plot_layout(guides = 'collect')
```

## Cluster proportions across age
Now we want to use our cluster assignments to see how strategies change throughout devoplment. These are plausibly quite non-linear age patterns, so we'll use GAMs.

```{r}
clust_long <- clust_map %>% 
  select(age.year, cluster_assignment) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = cluster_assignment,
              values_from = cluster_assignment,
              values_fn = length,
              values_fill = 0) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = Maximization:`Partner-Contingent Cooperation`,
               names_to = "cluster",
               values_to = "prop") %>% 
  mutate(cluster = factor(cluster,
                          levels = c("Maximization",
                                     "Generic Cooperation",
                                     "Partner-Contingent Cooperation"),
                          labels = c("Maximization",
                                     "Generic Cooperation",
                                     "Partner-Contingent Cooperation"))) %>%
  left_join(clust_map %>%
              select(pid, country)) %>% 
  unite("cluster_country", c(country, cluster), remove = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(cluster_country = factor(cluster_country),
         pid = factor(pid))


# fit a gamm
gam_clust <- gamm(prop ~ s(age.year, by = cluster, bs = "fs", k = 9) + cluster,
          # model assignment to a cluster using smoothed age for each cluster, cluster intercepts
          data = clust_long,
          random = list(pid = ~1), # subject level random effects for pooling and SEs
          method = "ML",
          family = binomial(link = "logit"))


gam.check(gam_clust$gam)
concurvity(gam_clust$gam, full = T)

# predict fit and get CIs
gam_pred <- predict(gam_clust$gam, newdata = clust_long, se.fit = TRUE, type = "response")

# tibble for plot
gam_plot <- tibble(
  age = clust_long$age.year,
  prop = clust_long$prop, 
  cluster = clust_long$cluster,
  fit = gam_pred$fit,
  ci_upper = gam_pred$fit + 1.96 * gam_pred$se.fit,
  ci_lower = gam_pred$fit - 1.96 * gam_pred$se.fit
)

clust_dev <- ggplot(gam_plot, aes(x = age, y = prop, group = cluster, color = cluster)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lower,
                  ymax = ci_upper),
              alpha = 0.2,
              fill = "grey",
              color = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit)) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 9) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = "Percentage in cluster", x = "Age", color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = c(.55, .85),
        legend.background = element_blank())
  

clust_country
clust_dev

```

## Cluster proportions across age and country
Of course, age trends might vary across societies, so we'll look at how the prevalence of each strategy changes across development for each of our societies.

```{r}
          data = clust_long,

)
```

# ------- RQ3: DO ADULT NORMS PREDICT CHILDREN'S BEHAVIOR BY AGE?

## ADULT NORMS
## Descriptives & Overview

```{r loading adult data}
adultnorms <-  read_csv("adultnorms_mar12.csv", na = "") 

#adultnorms %>% 
 # select(70:115) %>% 
 # mutate(location = tolower(location))

```



```{r descriptives}
# Sample sizes by country
adultnorms %>% 
 # group_by(country) %>% 
  tally()

# Gender by country 
adultnorms %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% 
  tally()


adultnorms %>% 
 # group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(tibble(mean.age= mean(age.year), sd.age = sd(age.year)))

adultnorms %>% 
  group_by(audio) %>% 
  tally()

str(adultnorms$country)
adultnorms$country <- factor(adultnorms$country, 
                               levels = c("Ecuador", "Peru", "Uganda", "Canada", "USA"))

```



Variables of interest: (all for adult recipient & actor)

* inequity_1v1 = should actor accept a split of 1 vs 1 (y/n) (equal)
* inequity_2v1 = should actor accept a split of 2 vs 1 (y/n)
* inequity_3v1 = should actor accept a split of 3 vs 1 (y/n)
* inequity_4v1 = should actor accept a split of 4 vs 1 (y/n) (standard AI)
* inequity_4v0 = should actor accept a split of 4 vs 0 (y/n) (extreme AI)
* inequity_1v4_di = should actor accept a split of 1 vs 4 (y/n) (standard DI)
* fairness.norm = how should actor split 4 candies? (numeric)
* trust.norm = how should actor split 6 fruits? (numeric)
* forgiveness.norm = how many sheets should actor give back? (numeric)
* honesty.norm = how many gifts should the actor keep? (numeric)
* honesty.num



## XAI Variation in adults

```{r}


str(adultnorms$inequity_4v0)
table(adultnorms$inequity_4v0)

adultnorms$inequity_4v0 <- gsub("N", "1", adultnorms$inequity_4v0)
adultnorms$inequity_4v0 <- as.numeric(adultnorms$inequity_4v0)

inequity.summary.4v0.adult <- summarySE(data = adultnorms,
                         measurevar = "inequity_4v0",
                         groupvars = c("country"),
                         na.rm = T)
inequity.summary.4v0.adult

summary(xai.adult.norm.mod <- lm(inequity_4v0 ~ country, data = adultnorms))
## Ecuador adult norms significantly different than others
```


## Calculating Difference Scores — Child Behavior & Adult Norms

```{r}

## Appending adult norm values to the dataset
### TRUST
x$adultnorm.trust.mean <- NA
x$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="USA", 2.75, NA)
x$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Canada", 2.31, x$adultnorm.trust.mean)
x$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Uganda", 3.27, x$adultnorm.trust.mean)
x$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Peru", 3.22, x$adultnorm.trust.mean)
x$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Ecuador", 3.46, x$adultnorm.trust.mean)


x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- NA
x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="USA", 4.6, NA)
x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Canada", 4.77, x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)
x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Uganda", 3.59, x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)
x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Peru", 3.78, x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)
x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Ecuador", 3.77, x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)


## These are "number you should return".
x$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- NA
x$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="USA", 2.6, NA)
x$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Canada", 2.38, x$adultnorm.honesty.mean)
x$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Uganda", 2.45, x$adultnorm.honesty.mean)
x$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Peru", 2.39, x$adultnorm.honesty.mean)
x$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(x$country=="Ecuador", 1.15, x$adultnorm.honesty.mean)


## Proportion of adults saying you should reject Standard AI
x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- NA
x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(x.long$country=="USA", .75, NA)
x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(x.long$country=="Canada", 1.0, x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)
x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(x.long$country=="Uganda", 0.68, x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)
x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(x.long$country=="Peru", 0.83, x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)
x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(x.long$country=="Ecuador", 0.38, x.long$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)



## Proportion of adults saying you should reject Extreme AI
adultnorms %>% 
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(tibble(extreme_ai_adult_mean= mean(inequity_4v0), extreme_ai_adult_sd = sd(inequity_4v0)))


x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean <- NA
x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(x$country=="USA", .9, NA)
x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(x$country=="Canada", .923, x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )
x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(x$country=="Uganda", 0.818, x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )
x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(x$country=="Peru", 0.889, x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )
x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(x$country=="Ecuador", 0.385, x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )

```



```{r}
## Creating Difference Scores
x$trust.diff.score <- abs(x$adultnorm.trust.mean - x$trust.numshared)
x$honesty.diff.score <- abs(x$adultnorm.honesty.mean - x$honesty.numreturned)
## both reciprocal, "number you should return", all good

x$forgive.diff.score <- abs(x$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean - x$forg.givenback)

x$xai.diff.score <- abs(x$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean - x$tt7.rejects)

x.long.2 <- x.long %>% 
  group_by(pid) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(dist == "AI") %>% 
  mutate(pid2 = pid) %>% 
  mutate(ai.average.choice = mean(dec)) %>% 
   mutate(ai.diff.score = abs(adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean - ai.average.choice))

 

## So now we have trust.diff.score, honesty.diff.score, forgive.diff.score, ai.diff.score, and xai.diff.score
```

## Difference Score Model: TRUST ADULT NORM | CHILD BEHAVIOR
```{r}
## TRUST

trust.diff.mod <-  
  lm(trust.diff.score ~  age.year*country, data = x)
summary(trust.diff.mod)

trust.diff.mod2 <-  
  lm(trust.diff.score ~  age.year + country, data = x)
summary(trust.diff.mod2)

anova(trust.diff.mod, trust.diff.mod2, test = "Chisq")
## sig. two way interaction between age and country
```

## HONESTY - ADULT NORMS

```{r}

str(adultnorms$honesty.norm)
table(adultnorms$honesty.norm)

honesty.summary.adult <- summarySE(data = adultnorms,
                         measurevar = "honesty.norm",
                         groupvars = c("country"),
                         na.rm = T)
honesty.summary.adult
# Norm for number of gifts you should keep out of four



## creating reciprocal
adultnorms$honesty.numreturned <- 4 -  adultnorms$honesty.norm

honesty.summary.adult.numreturned <- summarySE(data = adultnorms,
                         measurevar = "honesty.numreturned",
                         groupvars = c("country"),
                         na.rm = T)
honesty.summary.adult.numreturned
## Norm for number of gifts you should give back

## HONESTY NUMBER YOU SHOULD RETURN
honesty.means.adult.numreturned <- ggplot(honesty.summary.adult.numreturned, aes(x=country, y=honesty.numreturned, fill=country)) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=honesty.numreturned-se, ymax=honesty.numreturned+se), width=.2,
                position=position_dodge(.9)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",
           alpha = 0.6) + 
  xlab("\n Country") +
  ylab("Number You Should Return \n") + theme_gray() + guides(fill=FALSE) + 
  theme(text = element_text(size=19)) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  theme(text = element_text(size=19)) + ylim(0,4) #+ 
#gtitle("Honesty, Adult Norms")
honesty.means.adult.numreturned

```

# ------- RQ4: DO ADULT NORMS PREDICT CHILDREN'S NORMS?
## CHILD NORM BATTERY


```{r loading child norm battery  data}
childnorms <- read_csv("childnorms_mar12.csv", na = "")
# Tally
childnorms %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% 
  tally()

childnorms %>% 
  group_by(country, gender) %>% 
  tally()

childnorms %>% 
  #group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(tibble(mean.age= mean(age.year), sd.age = sd(age.year)))


```


```{r child norm basics}
table(childnorms$gender)
childnorms$male0 <- childnorms$gender
childnorms$male0 <- gsub("M", "0", childnorms$male0)
childnorms$male0 <- gsub("m", "0", childnorms$male0)
childnorms$male0 <- gsub("F", "1", childnorms$male0)
childnorms$male0 <- gsub("f", "1", childnorms$male0)
childnorms$male0 <- as.numeric(childnorms$male0)
table(childnorms$male0)


table(childnorms$country) 
table(childnorms$age.year) 

str(childnorms$country) 
childnorms$country <- factor(childnorms$country,  
                           levels = c("Ecuador", "Peru", "Uganda", "Canada", "USA" ))

```




## Calculating Difference Scores — Child Norms & Adult Norms

```{r}

## Appending adult norm values to the dataset
### TRUST
childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean <- NA
childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="USA", 2.75, NA)
childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Canada", 2.31, childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Uganda", 3.27, childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Peru", 3.22, childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Ecuador", 3.46, childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean)


childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- NA
childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="USA", 4.6, NA)
childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Canada", 4.77, childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Uganda", 3.59, childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Peru", 3.78, childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Ecuador", 3.77, childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean)


## Number you should RETURN
childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- NA
childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="USA", 2.6, NA)
childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Canada", 2.38, childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Uganda", 2.45, childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Peru", 2.39, childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Ecuador", 1.15, childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean)


## Proportion of adults saying you should reject Standard AI
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- NA
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="USA", .75, NA)
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Canada", 1.0, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Uganda", 0.68, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Peru", 0.83, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Ecuador", 0.38, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean)



## Proportion of adults saying you should reject Extreme AI
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean <- NA
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="USA", .9, NA)
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Canada", .923, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Uganda", 0.818, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Peru", 0.889, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )
childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean  <- ifelse(childnorms$country=="Ecuador", 0.385, childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean )


```



```{r}
## Creating Difference Scores
childnorms$trust.diff.score <- abs(childnorms$adultnorm.trust.mean - childnorms$trust.norms)


childnorms$honesty.number.returned <- 4 - childnorms$honesty.norms
childnorms$honesty.diff.score <- abs(childnorms$adultnorm.honesty.mean - childnorms$honesty.number.returned)
## Adults and children reciprocally coded as "number you should RETURN" (e.g. ECU ADULT = 1.15)

childnorms$forgive.diff.score <- abs(childnorms$adultnorm.forgiveness.mean - childnorms$forgiveness.norms)


## here, childnorms$ai_yesno is coded as saying "y" or "n" to the decision
## So we need to recode and make it a numeric variable


childnorms$ai_yesno <- gsub("Y", "0", childnorms$ai_yesno)
childnorms$ai_yesno <- gsub("N", "1", childnorms$ai_yesno)
childnorms$ai_yesno <- as.numeric(childnorms$ai_yesno)

childnorms.ai_yesno.summary <- summarySE(data = childnorms,
                         measurevar = "ai_yesno",
                         groupvars = c("country"),
                         na.rm = T)
childnorms.ai_yesno.summary

childnorms$ai.diff.score <- abs(childnorms$adultnorm.inequityAI4v1.mean - childnorms$ai_yesno)

## same recording for xai
childnorms$`4 v. 0` <- gsub("Y", "0", childnorms$`4 v. 0`)
childnorms$`4 v. 0` <- gsub("y", "0", childnorms$`4 v. 0`)
childnorms$`4 v. 0` <- gsub("N", "1", childnorms$`4 v. 0`)
childnorms$`4 v. 0` <- gsub("n", "1", childnorms$`4 v. 0`)
childnorms$`4 v. 0` <- as.numeric(childnorms$`4 v. 0`)
childnorms$xai.diff.score <- abs(childnorms$adultnorm.inequityextremeAI.mean - 
                                   childnorms$`4 v. 0`)
```

#### Uganda
```{r}


## INEQUITY AVERSION
## KIDS NORM AS A DASHED LINE
## KIDS BEHAVIOR AS A STRAIGHT LINE
## ADULT NORM AS A POINTRANGE

just.uganda.ai.child <- ai.summary.2.child %>% 
  filter(., country == "Uganda") 


## plotting kids' norms
just.uganda.ai <-  ggplot(data = just.uganda.ai.child, aes(x=age.year, y=ai_yesno)) + 
  geom_smooth(data = just.uganda.ai.child , method = "lm", fill = color.Uganda, alpha = 0.09, linetype = 0) +
  geom_line(data= just.uganda.ai.child , stat = "smooth", linetype = "dotted",
            method = "lm", size=1, color = color.Uganda) +
  xlab("\n Age") +
  ylab("Proportion Rejecting AI \n") + theme_gray() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
   ylim(-0.4,1.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(6, 8, 10, 12))
just.uganda.ai


inequity.summary.4v1.adult3 <- inequity.summary.4v1.adult
inequity.summary.4v1.adult3$age.year <- 14
inequity.summary.4v1.adult3 <- rename(inequity.summary.4v1.adult3, ai_yesno = inequity_4v1)


just.uganda.ai.adult <- 
   inequity.summary.4v1.adult3 %>% 
  filter(., country == "Uganda")


## so now we have a graph that's adult norms in a pointrange, and kid norms as a line
just.uganda.superimposed <- just.uganda.ai + 
  geom_pointrange(data=just.uganda.ai.adult, 
                  fatten = 1,
                  size = 2,
                  aes(ymin=ai_yesno-se, ymax=ai_yesno+se),
                  position=position_dodge(width=1),
                  color = color.Uganda) + theme(legend.position = "none") 
just.uganda.superimposed



just.uganda.ai.kids <- ai.only %>% 
  filter(country == "Uganda") %>% 
  rename(., ai_yesno = dec)

## now adding in kids' behavior
# putting it all together
ai.Uganda.final <- just.uganda.superimposed +
  geom_smooth(data = just.uganda.ai.kids, alpha=0.2, method = "lm",  fill = color.Uganda) +
  geom_line(data=just.uganda.ai.kids, stat = "smooth", method = "lm",  size=1,  color = color.Uganda) +
  ggtitle("AI - Uganda")

ai.Uganda.final  


```

```{r}
  filter(., country == "Canada") 
just.Canada.honesty.child


just.Canada.honesty <-  ggplot(data = just.Canada.honesty.child, 
                               aes(x=age.year, y= honesty.number.returned)) + 
  geom_smooth(data = just.Canada.honesty.child, 
              fill = color.Canada, 
              method = "lm", 
              alpha = 0.09, 
              linetype = 0) +
  geom_line(data= just.Canada.honesty.child, 
            stat = "smooth", 
            linetype = "dotted",
            method = "lm", 
            color = color.Canada, 
            size = 1) +
  xlab("\n Age") +
  ylab("Number Returned \n") + theme_gray() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(6, 8, 10, 12))
just.Canada.honesty



just.Canada.honesty.adult <- 
   honesty.summary.adult.numreturned4 %>% 
  filter(., country == "Canada")


## so now we have a graph that's adult norms in a pointrange, and kid norms as a line
just.Canada.superimposed.honesty <- just.Canada.honesty + 
  geom_pointrange(data=just.Canada.honesty.adult, 
                  aes(ymin=honesty.number.returned-se, ymax=honesty.number.returned+se),
                  position=position_dodge(width=1),
                  fatten = 1,
                  size = 2,
                  color = color.Canada) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
just.Canada.superimposed.honesty



just.Canada.honesty.kids <- honesty.kidsbehavior.summary %>% 
  filter(country == "Canada")

## now adding in kids' behavior

honesty.Canada.final <- just.Canada.superimposed.honesty +
  geom_smooth(data = just.Canada.honesty.kids, 
              alpha=0.2, 
              fill = color.Canada, 
              method = "lm") +
  geom_line(data=just.Canada.honesty.kids, 
            stat = "smooth", 
            method = "lm", 
            color = color.Canada, 
            size = 1) +
  ggtitle("Honesty - Canada")

honesty.Canada.final
```
